name: Table for Twenty
subject: Hamptons restaurants
tagline: Eleven questions on the places you've waited an hour for, from lobster shacks to the wood-fired room everyone pretends not to look around. A theme the crew voted for.

questions.q: The roadside lobster-roll place on the Napeague stretch in Amagansett, open since 1965, is known by the one word on its sign. What is it?
questions.w: Lunch. The Lobster Roll restaurant put the word on its roof in the 1960s and the nickname stuck.
questions.more: It began as a hot-dog stand called the Lunch Box before switching to lobster, and it claims to have been serving lobster rolls on Long Island before anyone else. Its exterior stood in for a diner in the television series The Affair. Across the road, the Clam Bar on Napeague has run the same open-air act since 1980.

questions.q: Which East Hampton restaurant, opened in 1988 with a wood-burning oven, is the one where people go to see who else is there?
questions.w: Nick & Toni's, opened by Jeff Salaway and the artist Toni Ross on North Main Street.
questions.more: Its rustic Italian menu and the oven gave the Hamptons a template copied for decades, and its regulars over the years have included Steven Spielberg, Billy Joel and Alec Baldwin. Salaway died in a car crash in 2001; Ross and the chef Joe Realmuto have run it since, and the garden out back supplies the kitchen. The same group runs La Fondita and Rowdy Hall.

questions.q: Which Southampton bakery's chocolate chip cookies started in a farm stand and ended up in supermarkets nationwide?
questions.w: Tate's Bake Shop, founded by Kathleen King, who sold cookies at her family's farm stand from the age of eleven.
questions.more: She named the shop after her father in 2000 after losing her first bakery in a business dispute. The thin, crisp cookies in the green bag were bought by the snack giant Mondelēz in 2018 for about 500 million dollars. The original shop on North Sea Road still draws a line on summer mornings.

questions.q: Gosman's, the sprawling dock-side spot at the Montauk harbor mouth, began life in 1943 as what?
o: A fish market and chowder stand
questions.w: A chowder stand and fish market, run by Robert and Mary Gosman on the inlet.
questions.more: The family grew it into a restaurant, a clam bar, a fish market and a row of shops, and the deck became the place to watch the boats come in. It has stayed in the Gosman family for three generations, and the fishing fleet still unloads yards away.

questions.q: Round Swamp Farm, the farm stand on Three Mile Harbor Road in East Hampton, is famous for charging what kind of prices?
o: Cash only, one dollar an item
questions.w: High ones, and happily paid: a famous local joke is that a bag of its muffins and chicken salad costs more than dinner elsewhere.
questions.more: The stand grew out of a Bonacker family's farm and fishing, and the pies, cookies, salads and fresh fish are made on the premises. It is a Hamptons rite to complain about the bill in the car park and be back the next morning. There is a second stand in Bridgehampton.

questions.q: Duryea's Lobster Deck, the Montauk fish house with the sunset views over Fort Pond Bay, was bought in 2014 by which financier, who turned it into a polished scene?
questions.w: Marc Rowan, co-founder of the private-equity firm Apollo, who owns a house nearby.
questions.more: The Duryea family had run it as a plain lobster deck since the 1930s. Rowan's makeover brought rosé by the glass, linen napkins and a long fight with the town over permits for a seating deck that had grown without them, which ran for years and became a symbol of new Montauk versus old. He later opened a second Duryea's in Orient.

questions.q: Sant Ambroeus, the café and restaurant on Main Street in Southampton that serves cappuccinos to the linen-shirt set, started where?
questions.w: Milan, as a pasticceria opened in 1936. The Southampton branch came in 1992.
questions.more: The name is Milan's patron saint, Ambrose. The New York branches on Madison Avenue and in the West Village and SoHo made it the lunch spot of the art and fashion crowd, and the Southampton one brought the same panettone and pink boxes to the beach. It stays open all year, which in Southampton counts as a civic service.

questions.q: Which Bridgehampton luncheonette, with its counter stools and homemade ice cream, has been on the Main Street corner since 1925?
questions.w: Candy Kitchen, run by the Laggis family since the 1980s, where the breakfast crowd includes farmers, surfers and the odd billionaire.
questions.more: It opened the year after the Bridgehampton road races began and has outlasted most of the shops around it. Sip 'n Soda is its Southampton cousin, opened by the Parash family in 1958 and still making its own ice cream and egg creams. Golden Pear is the coffee-and-muffin chain with branches across the villages.

questions.q: Wölffer Estate in Sagaponack, whose rosé is the unofficial drink of a Hamptons summer, was founded by which German-born businessman?
questions.w: Christian Wölffer, who bought a potato farm in 1978 for horses and planted vines in 1988.
questions.more: He died in a swimming accident in Brazil in 2008, and his children Marc and Joey run the estate with the winemaker Roman Roth. Its Summer in a Bottle rosé, with the flowered label, sells hundreds of thousands of cases, and the wine stand on Montauk Highway is where sunset drinks happen on Fridays.

questions.q: Dreesen's, the East Hampton market whose doughnuts have been a local institution since the 1950s, closed in 2002. Where did its doughnut machine go?
o: Scoop du Jour, the ice-cream shop on Newtown Lane
questions.w: Scoop du Jour, which still makes Dreesen's doughnuts on the old machine every morning.
questions.more: Dreesen's Excelsior Market had been on Newtown Lane since the 1920s, selling meat and groceries to summer houses before the doughnuts took over its fame. When the family closed the market, the machine and the recipe went two doors down, and the line of damp children and dogs outside Scoop du Jour on a summer morning is unchanged.

questions.q: Which of these are in Montauk? Select all that apply.
o: The Hideaway, the Mexican place on the marina
questions.w: The Hideaway, Duryea's and Montauk Brewing are in Montauk. The Clam Bar is on the Napeague stretch in Amagansett, and Sip 'n Soda is in Southampton.
questions.more: Montauk Brewing opened in 2012 in a garage on South Erie Avenue and its Wave Chaser IPA is now sold across the Northeast. The Hideaway sits at the Montauk Marine Basin, where you eat tacos looking at sport-fishing boats. The town line between Amagansett and Montauk runs through the empty dunes of Napeague, which is why everyone argues about where the Clam Bar is.
